claims.evidence: Python blindness is real and reproduced by me on the same files: for all 17 files in the two target folders, os.stat().st_file_attributes == 0x20 (python_0x400=0, python_0x20=17) while PowerShell (Get-Item -Force).Attributes.value__ == 0x420 (ps_0x400=17) and fsutil reparsepoint query returns 'Reparse Tag Value : 0x9000601a' (tag_ok=17). I extended the check to a 5,000-file walk of C:\Users\郑曾波\Dropbox\Stock: python_0x400_found=0, while every ~500th file sampled with PowerShell reported 0x420 (e.g. '视觉中国：2020年第一季度报告全文.PDF' py=0x20 ps=0x420). GetFileInformationByHandleEx(FileBasicInfo) also reports 0x20 for the targets, so the blindness covers the raw Win32 basic-info path too. The tag is decisive: 0x9000601a with reparse data magic 'FeRp' (Dropbox), and fsutil's own 'Tag value: Microsoft' names a vendor owner while 'Tag value: Directory' is the name-surrogate flag, not a claim that the target is a directory. The fix is sound: the PowerShell discriminator (value & 0x400) selects Dropbox's cloud-file shape on this host. The control was re-run by me and printed files=17 reparse=17 plain=0.
claims.note: Blindness is general within the Dropbox tree but CONDITIONAL overall, which the record should say explicitly: off the Dropbox tree python and PowerShell agree - on the junction C:\Users\郑曾波\AppData\Local\History python's st_file_attributes = 0x2416 (bit 0x400 True, os.path.isjunction True) while powershell also says 0x2416, and on a normal local file (revenue-forecast\SKILL.md) both say 0x20. That strengthens the finding (it is a Dropbox/cloud-shape blindness, not a broken Python) and also means the invariant name 'python_instrument_disagrees_with_fsutil' is exactly right. I could NOT independently confirm the FIRST version's literal output ('placeholders_before: 0' / 'hydration_observed: 0'): that artifact is not in the run directory - only the references to it (json summary.withdrawn_claim, md:10-11, findings.md:32 F-BAR-13, progress.md:8). But the withdrawal is correct on its merits: any hydration verdict derived from the 0x400 bit of st_file_attributes is necessarily vacuous here.

claims.evidence: True part: every entry carries data_locality_determinable=false (3/3), and neither the prose nor the JSON asserts that hydration happened or did not happen (the withdrawn numbers survive only inside summary.withdrawn_claim / the harness docstring, explicitly marked WITHDRAWN). False part: data locality IS determinable with standard, read-only, non-hydrating Win32 calls on this host. GetFileInformationByHandleEx(FileStandardInfo) via a handle opened with ZERO desired access returns AllocationSize adjacent to EndOfFile. For the three targets: alloc=4096 vs eof=567, alloc=4096 vs eof=567, alloc=4096 vs eof=543 - the data is present locally in full (a not-locally-present file reports alloc==0 for its data); and for the sample I scanned, alloc is 0 files out of 17 in those two folders, i.e. no dry file exists there at all.
claims.note: So the record under-claims rather than over-claims: 'this run cannot say whether the read hydrated the file' is too strong, because the locality question is answerable with metadata only (prose sect.3 itself names 'GetFileInformationByHandleEx 的 FileStandardInfo' as the tool it would need - and that call is available here without opening the data). The correction direction is safe (no unproven hydration assertion survives), but the justification for the disclaimer is inaccurate and the harness could have carried a real pre/post locality reading instead of a blanket false.

findings.statement: The record declares data locality undeterminable ('data_locality_determinable: false' x3, md sect.3 'existing three instruments cannot answer whether the data was local before the read'), but locality is determinable on this host with a metadata-only call the harness never made: GetFileInformationByHandleEx(FileStandardInfo).AllocationSize. Measured: the three targets report AllocationSize 4096/4096/4096 against EndOfFile 567/567/543, i.e. the bytes were already fully resident locally; across all 17 files of the two folders alloc==0 occurs 0 times. The system under review therefore under-claims, and the artifact's central open question was answerable.
findings.evidence: run_r5_dropbox_bytes.py:351-357 sets data_locality_determinable=false with the note 'NOT determinable with these instruments'; b-ar-dropbox-bytes.md:57-58 names the right tool ('GetFileInformationByHandleEx 的 FileStandardInfo') as the thing it lacks. My measurement (ctypes CreateFileW with dwDesiredAccess=0, FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS, then GetFileInformationByHandleEx(FileStandardInfo)): '紫金矿业...2024年年报报告.pdf.source.json alloc=4096 eof=567', '...2025年年度报告.pdf.source.json alloc=4096 eof=567', '星环科技：2024年年度报告.pdf.source.json alloc=4096 eof=543'; whole-folder scan: TOTALS {"n": 17, "alloc_zero": 0, "alloc_gt0": 17}. Control that the call itself reads nothing: the handle is opened with zero desired access, so it cannot trigger a recall.
findings.why_it_matters: The step's headline honesty claim is 'we cannot tell whether the read hydrated the files'. A buyer of this record would conclude the dropbox_stock side-effect question is permanently unanswerable, when in fact (a) the data was already local, and (b) a pre/post AllocationSize reading would have given the harness the hydration signal it says it lacks. This is the difference between 'hydration is unmeasurable' and 'hydration did not need to happen'.

findings.statement: The before/after state fingerprint omits the one cheap metadata channel that catches metadata-only mutation - NTFS ChangeTime (GetFileInformationByHandleEx(FileBasicInfo)) - so 'state_changes_observed: 0' and 'no_size_change_observed: true' are vacuously strong: they cannot register a change that leaves size, mtime, attribute value and reparse tag intact. On these very files that channel is non-trivial: ChangeTime is recent (2026-09-18T19:11:22Z for both 紫金矿业 sidecars, 2026-09-18T18:49:47Z for the 星环 sidecar) while LastWriteTime is still 2026-08-10T20:42:54Z and never moved.
findings.evidence: run_r5_dropbox_bytes.py:341-350 compares python_attributes, powershell value, fsutil tag, size, mtime - nothing else; the invariant at :405-407 is literally a size comparison. Measured live: 星环科技：2024年年度报告.pdf.source.json {created 2026-08-10T20:11:49Z, last_write 2026-08-10T20:42:54Z, change 2026-09-18T18:49:47Z}; 紫金矿业 2024 sidecar {last_write 2026-08-10T20:42:54Z, change 2026-09-18T19:11:22Z}; 紫金矿业 2025 sidecar {change 2026-09-18T19:11:22Z}; R5 ran_at_utc = 2026-09-18T19:14:08Z.
findings.why_it_matters: The run window was demonstrably not quiet (something re-stamped these files' change times minutes before the run, and my own read moved LastAccessTime to 19:16:24-25Z), yet the harness's fingerprint would have printed 'no state change observed' either way. A record whose no-write leg rests on a fingerprint with a known blind spot should say so - the more so because the omitted reading is one API call away and costs nothing.

findings.evidence: run_r5_dropbox_bytes.py:70-74 PLACEHOLDER_FLAGS is defined but never evaluated against any measurement (grep: the dict is only declared; is_cloud_file is computed from fsutil at :331); record state_before/state_after powershell.value == 1056 (0x420) for all three entries; my folder scan shows item_attrs 1056 for all 17 items; 0x1000/0x40000/0x400000 appear in none of the readings.
findings.why_it_matters: A dead heuristic documented as the discriminator invites the next reader (or the next tool) to key the hydration guard on flags that are never present in this tree, which is the failure mode B.AR's own path-substring guard already exhibited (b-ar-record.md:87, B-VR-BAR-05).
